newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs weak after Nissan Life news.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs weak after Nissan Life news.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were hit by waves of selling on Friday following news a medium-sized Japanese life insurance company was to be liquidated.
Japan's Finance Ministry ordered Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co to halt operations, sparking fears the company might be forced to sell some of its bond holdings.

"A good part of the assets held by the life insurance company are JGBs. People are afraid they might have to dispose these off and that's why JGBs went into a free fall," a trader with a European bank said.
A dealer with a European futures house said Nissan Life was believed to hold an estimated 300 billion yen worth of JGBs and 700 billion yen worth of foreign bonds.

June JGBs fell to a low of 125.25 in afternoon trade as news of Nissan Life's failure triggered concerns of higher interest rates. Japan's low-rate environment has been blamed for weak returns on financial institutions' investments.
June JGBs ended at 125.57 against their previous 126.58.
"Everyone in Japan, except the banks would be happier with higher rates," the bank dealer said.

"There's little reason to buy this market now so people will sell into any rallies. The market is pricing in the possibility of higher rates but I'm still not sure they'll raise rates this year," he said.

He said December Euroyen was headed for an objective of 98.90 while any upside would be capped at 99.03. The contract stood at 98.96 at 1115 GMT after falling as low as 98.95 against an IMM close at 99.04. Turnover was a healthy 27,210 lots.
A trader with a Japanese futures house said the market had over-reacted to the news as Japan was in no position to raise rates while its banking sector remained in dire straits.
"It's a relatively small insurance company and shouldn't be having this kind of impact," he said, pointing to the Finance Ministry's assurance that Nissan Life was an isolated incident.
Eurodollar futures ended easier as expectations of higher U.S. rates continued to weigh on the market.
"Most Federal Reserve officials are still claiming the economy is doing well, that it's good to be pre-emptive on inflation," the bank dealer said.
He added that the market would keep a close watch on next week's first quarter U.S. Employment Cost Index for indications of inflationary pressures.
September Eurodollars ended at 93.675 against their IMM close at 93.690 on volume of 9,875 lots.
